title: To the church at Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1–17)
hook: a messy church split into fan clubs: I follow Paul, I Apollos
tomorrow: why would Paul admit his message sounds foolish?

segments.voice: Acts ended in a hired house in Rome, the chain on and the door open. The line: no man forbidding him.

Teams pick favorite coaches. Group chats split over who's right. Acts is done, and the letters begin with a church doing exactly that. Word reaches Paul from Chloe's people that Corinth is quarreling: "Every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ." Fan clubs. So whose club does Paul go after first? His own.
screen: `TEAM THIS ONE, TEAM THAT ONE.` → `I AM OF PAUL, I OF APOLLOS.` → `HIS OWN CLUB, FIRST.`

segments.voice: Today's question: what holds a group together when people love different leaders? Paul starts by calling this quarreling church "the church of God which is at Corinth" and its people saints. Then the plea: "that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you". Then three questions: "Is Christ divided? was Paul crucified for you? or were ye baptized in the name of Paul?" He won't let his name be a team jersey. He's glad he baptized hardly any of them, then, mid-letter, can't quite remember: "besides, I know not whether I baptized any other." The names were never the point. The center is Christ, crucified for them. A neighbor tradition worries about the same split. The Qur'an tells believers to hold fast, all together, to the rope of God, and not to break into factions. That's shared ground: a community stays one by holding the same thing, not by picking a favorite person. And the honest difference: Paul's center is Christ, the name they were baptized into. In the Qur'an the rope is God's, and Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet, not as the Lord Paul names. Same worry about splitting. A different center.
screen: `WHAT HOLDS A GROUP TOGETHER?` · `IS CHRIST DIVIDED?` · `THE QUR'AN: HOLD FAST TOGETHER.` · `SAME WORRY, DIFFERENT CENTER.` · then, large: `IS CHRIST DIVIDED?`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a group you're in where people have quietly picked sides. Count three people in it you're grateful for, and make sure they aren't all from your side. Name each one, and one thing they bring.
To the church at Corinth. A letter to a quarreling church, addressed to people Paul still calls saints.

segments.voice: Your line: is Christ divided? Paul asks it of a church split into fan clubs, his own included. Day done.

fork.setup: a friend says the Qur'an's 'hold the rope together' proves every religion teaches the same thing. what's the fairest reply?
options: both warn against splitting; the honest difference is the center.

fork.reveal: shared ground is real: hold together, don't split. so is the difference: Paul's center is Christ; the Qur'an's rope is God's. neither ranks the other.

chat.meaning: Paul and the Qur'an share the worry about splitting into factions. The honest difference is the center: Christ for Paul, God's rope for the Qur'an.

Corinth.meaning: a Greek city whose church Paul wrote to

Apollos.meaning: a gifted teacher Priscilla and Aquila once took aside

Cephas.meaning: another name for the apostle Peter

Chloe.meaning: a woman whose people told Paul about the quarrels

notes: Recipe v3, wisdom shape with the unity thread: the question (what holds a group together when people love different leaders?), Paul's answer, and one neighbor: Qur'an 3:103, paraphrased (not quoted) as 'hold fast, all together, to the rope of God, and not break into factions'. Pickthall 1930 renders it 'the cable of Allah'; the lesson paraphrases to stay safe. Honest difference: Paul's center is Christ; in the Qur'an the rope is God's, and Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet. Please have a Muslim reviewer confirm the paraphrase and that the difference is fairly put; nothing ranked, never 'all the same'.
1 Corinthians 1:12 in the KJV begins 'Now this I say, that every one of you saith'; the hook quotes from 'Every one'.
'Cephas: another name for the apostle Peter' rests on John 1:42; Apollos's link to Priscilla and Aquila rests on Acts 18:24–28 (day 1518).
Crispus and Gaius (1:14) appear in the match game; the household of Stephanas (1:16) is left out of the voice for length.
